questions.q: What is the core difference between request-response and event-driven interaction?
options: Request-response only works inside Salesforce; event-driven only works with external systems
In request-response the caller waits for a direct answer; in event-driven, a publisher announces a fact and moves on without waiting for anyone to react
Event-driven systems never involve Apex code
Request-response is always faster than event-driven messaging
questions.explain: Request-response blocks the caller on a direct answer. Event-driven publishing announces something that already happened and continues, regardless of who (if anyone) reacts.

questions.q: Which of these is the best example of an 'event' in the event-driven sense?
options: "Please create a new Case for this customer"
"Order #4521 just shipped"
"Return the balance of Account 001"
"Run this batch job every night at 2 AM"
questions.explain: An event describes a fact that already happened, in the past tense. The other options are a command, a query, and a schedule — not events.

questions.q: In the publish/subscribe pattern, who decides whether and how to react to an event?
options: The publisher decides, and tells each subscriber directly what to do
A central administrator manually routes each event to the correct system
Each subscriber decides independently, and the publisher doesn't need to know which subscribers exist
Only one subscriber is allowed to listen to a given channel at a time
questions.explain: Subscribers independently decide how to react. The publisher puts the event on a channel and is done — it doesn't address the event to a specific recipient or know who's listening.

questions.q: Why does polling a REST API every few minutes fall short as a substitute for an event-driven notification?
options: REST APIs cannot return JSON
Polling wastes API calls, adds latency, and can still miss a change that happens and reverses between polls
Polling is only possible from inside Salesforce
REST APIs do not support authentication
questions.explain: Periodic polling trades real-time awareness for wasted calls and the risk of missing short-lived changes that occur and revert between poll intervals — a gap event-driven delivery closes.

questions.q: What does 'decoupling' mean in the context of publishers and subscribers?
options: Publishers and subscribers must always be deployed in the same release
A subscriber being offline blocks the publisher from doing its own work
Publishers and subscribers can be added, changed, or taken offline independently, without the other side needing to know or change
Only Apex triggers can act as publishers
questions.explain: Decoupling means the publisher and subscriber don't need to know about each other or be available at the same time — a new subscriber can start listening without any change to the publisher.
